svg.text: Per-cluster GCP project · same VPC pattern (custom-mode, single subnet, secondary ranges) · key difference: DEV runs DBs in-cluster · PROD reaches managed services via Service Networking VPC peering

g.text: Traffic legend
inbound HTTPS
egress to internet (via NAT)
egress to Google APIs (Private Google Access)
VPC peering (Service Networking)
Status
configured
partial / risk
critical / blocker
DEV CLUSTER · NETWORK
GCP project crego-app-dev · region asia-south1 · serves NS development + qa1 + qa2
Internet — End users / tenants
Per-tenant subdomains under *.dev.crego.app · HTTPS only
Tenant domains resolve to NGINX LB external IP via Cloud DNS
Operators — kubectl / IAP / ArgoCD UI
kubectl reaches the GKE control-plane PUBLIC endpoint over HTTPS
⚠ Master Authorized Networks (MAN) defaults to 0.0.0.0/0 — anyone with creds can reach the API
443/tcp
kube-apiserver 443
Inbound LB — NGINX Ingress Controller
Service type: LoadBalancer → external Premium-tier IP (regional)
cert-manager terminates TLS using LE certs (HTTP-01 challenge)
⚠ NGINX install not in GitOps · ⚠ default replica count = 1 (SPOF)
GKE Control-plane (Google-managed VPC)
Endpoint type: enable_private_endpoint=false (PUBLIC)
VPC peering CP ↔ nodes managed by GKE (transparent)
⚠⚠ MAN allow-list empty → bootstrap default 0.0.0.0/0 in bootstrap-gcp.sh
VPC: dev-vpc (custom mode, single regional subnet) · terraform/modules/gcp-vpc
Subnet: dev-subnet · region asia-south1 · Private Google Access: ON
Primary CIDR: 10.0.0.0/16 (nodes, internal LBs) · Pods (secondary): 10.4.0.0/14 · Services (secondary): 10.8.0.0/20
Secondary ranges allocated as IP-aliasing for GKE; up to ~65k pods · ~4k cluster IPs
GKE cluster — gke-dev (regional, private nodes)
Node pool: e2-standard-* · auto-repair / auto-upgrade · shielded (secure-boot + integrity)
Network Policy: ON (Calico/Dataplane-V2) · Workload Identity pool: crego-app-dev.svc.id.goog
Cluster DNS: kube-dns / NodeLocal DNSCache · Metadata server: GKE_METADATA mode
Pods (NS: development · qa1 · qa2)
Apps: omni-api, flow-api, omni-web, flow-web, flower
Workers: omni-celery-{worker,beat}, flow-celery-worker (KEDA-scaled)
In-cluster DBs: postgres · redis · rabbitmq · mongodb (PVC-backed)
⚠ Egress NetworkPolicy still allows 0.0.0.0/0 — no DNS/HTTPS-only filter
⚠ No Pod Security Admission labels on dev/qa1/qa2 namespaces
⚠⚠ Three NS share one cluster — no ResourceQuota / LimitRange in repo (noisy-neighbour risk)
Intra-cluster traffic
Pod-to-pod via service CIDR 10.8.0.0/20 · resolved by kube-dns
In-cluster DB hostnames: postgres.<ns>.svc.cluster.local etc.
⚠ allow-internal firewall rule permits ALL proto/ports inside subnet+pods+svc
Cloud Router + Cloud NAT
dev-router · dev-nat
NAT IP allocation: AUTO_ONLY (no reserved static IP)
Single regional NAT IP for all egress
Logs: errors only (cost-saving)
⚠ Auto IP — outbound IP can change; whitelist-by-IP partners will break
Private Google Access
DNS: private.googleapis.com via 199.36.153.8/30
Traffic to Google APIs stays on Google backbone
No external IP required on nodes
Used by ESO, GAR pulls, external-dns, Cloud Logging
VPC firewall rules (terraform/modules/gcp-vpc)
⚠⚠ allow-internal: ALL protocols/ports between subnet + pod + service CIDRs (over-broad)
✓ Implicit deny ingress from internet (no public IPs on nodes)
✓ GKE master ↔ nodes auto-managed (CP-to-node 443/tcp + 10250/tcp)
⚠ No egress firewall rules in repo — only NetworkPolicy at K8s layer (insufficient defence-in-depth)
In-cluster stateful (DEV-only pattern)
postgres · redis · rabbitmq · mongodb live INSIDE the cluster (no peering, no managed services)
Reached by apps via cluster-local DNS — never traverses VPC peering
⚠ DEV does not exercise the Service Networking peering path → PROD-specific bugs only surface in PROD
Google APIs & managed services (reached from VPC via Private Google Access)
Secret Manager (GSM): project crego-app-dev · keys app-dev / app-qa1 / app-qa2 — read by ESO via WI
Cloud DNS: zone for dev.crego.app — A records updated by external-dns (KSA → GSA external-dns-sa, role roles/dns.admin)
Artifact Registry / GCR: image pulls via Private Google Access
Cloud Logging / Monitoring: node SA writes logs & metrics (roles/logging.logWriter, monitoring.metricWriter)
⚠ No CMEK on GSM secrets · ⚠ No VPC Service Controls perimeter
to internet
PROD CLUSTER · NETWORK
GCP project crego-app-prod · region asia-south1 · NS production · PREPROD = identical topology in project crego-app-preprod
Internet — End users / tenants
Per-tenant subdomains under *.crego.app · HTTPS only
Resolves to global anycast IP crego-prod-ip
Operators — kubectl / IAP / ArgoCD UI
kubectl reaches the GKE control-plane PUBLIC endpoint over HTTPS
⚠⚠ Same MAN-default 0.0.0.0/0 in PROD — control plane is internet-exposed
443/tcp · global
kube-apiserver 443
Inbound LB — GKE Gateway API
Class: gke-l7-global-external-managed (Google Cloud Global LB)
Static external IP crego-prod-ip · NEG-backed → pod IPs · HTTPRoute injects HSTS/CSP/X-XSS
⚠ No Cloud Armor / WAF / rate-limit attached to backend
GKE Control-plane (Google-managed VPC)
Endpoint type: enable_private_endpoint=false (PUBLIC)
VPC peering CP ↔ nodes managed by GKE
⚠⚠ PROD CP reachable from anywhere on the internet
VPC: prod-vpc (custom mode, single regional subnet) · same Terraform module as DEV
Subnet: prod-subnet · region asia-south1 · Private Google Access: ON
Primary CIDR: 10.10.0.0/16 · Pods: 10.20.0.0/14 · Services: 10.24.0.0/20 (verify exact ranges in tfvars)
Service Networking peered range allocated for managed services (Cloud SQL + Memorystore)
GKE cluster — gke-prod (regional, private nodes)
Node pool: production-tier (verify in tfvars) · auto-repair / auto-upgrade · shielded
Network Policy: ON · WI pool: crego-app-prod.svc.id.goog
Cluster DNS: kube-dns · Metadata server: GKE_METADATA
Pods (NS: production)
Apps: omni-api · flow-api · omni-web · flow-web · flower
Workers: omni-celery-{worker,beat} · flow-celery-worker
⚠⚠ kustomize override forces replicas: 1 on every Deployment (defeats HPA)
⚠⚠ RabbitMQ STILL in-cluster (single replica) — managed services exclude RabbitMQ
Egress paths from pods
→ Internet: pod → Cloud NAT → regional NAT IP
→ Google APIs: pod → Private Google Access → googleapis.com
→ Managed data: pod → VPC peering → Cloud SQL / Memorystore (PRIVATE IPs only)
→ External MongoDB: egress via Cloud NAT (DSN injected via ESO)
⚠ Egress NetworkPolicy still allows 0.0.0.0/0
⚠ No PSA labels · ⚠ readOnlyRootFilesystem: false on api/web/worker
Service Networking
VPC peering: servicenetworking-googleapis-com
Reserved range allocated for managed services
Cloud SQL — Postgres
Private IP only · HA + PITR variable-driven
Module: terraform/modules/gcp-cloudsql-postgres
Memorystore — Redis
Private VPC peering · same region
Module: terraform/modules/gcp-redis
Cloud Router + Cloud NAT
prod-router · prod-nat · AUTO_ONLY
Single regional NAT IP for egress
⚠ Auto IP — outbound IP not stable
⚠ External MongoDB egress goes through this NAT IP
VPC firewall rules (same Terraform module as DEV)
⚠⚠ allow-internal: ALL protocols/ports between subnet + pod + service CIDRs
✓ Implicit deny ingress from internet
⚠⚠ Cloud SQL / Memorystore reachable from any pod (lateral-movement risk if app pod compromised)
⚠ Tighten to: TCP 5432 (SQL), 6379 (Redis), 5672/15672 (Rabbit), 27017 (Mongo), 53, 443 only
PROD addon gap (in-cluster networking implications)
⚠⚠ addons/prod-gcp/ contains ONLY external-secrets — no cert-manager, no external-dns, no KEDA
⚠ DNS records for new tenant subdomains likely managed manually (not via external-dns)
⚠ Edge TLS cert is GCP-managed via cert-map (not LE) — separate from cert-manager flow used in DEV
Google APIs & managed services (reached via Private Google Access or VPC peering)
Secret Manager (GSM): project crego-app-prod · key app-prod — ESO eso-sa KSA → GSA via WI
Cloud DNS: zone for crego.app — managed, but no external-dns to update records automatically (manual / Gateway-managed)
Artifact Registry: image pulls via Private Google Access · Cloud Logging: node SA writes logs/metrics
⚠⚠ No CMEK on GSM / PD-SSD / Cloud SQL · ⚠ No VPC Service Controls perimeter · ⚠ No K8s API audit log sink configured
⚠ Cloud SQL has Cross-region read-replica capability via Terraform (variable) but not enabled by default
to internet
PREPROD note — identical to PROD topology, except: project = crego-app-preprod · DBs are still IN-CLUSTER (no Cloud SQL / Memorystore peering) · ⚠⚠ this divergence breaks PRE as a release gate
